distinctions.bypass_reader_interface: Does not resolve downstream sign-sensitive consumers or provide a validated dataflow contract.
distinctions.downstream_algorithm_redesign: Would require reviewed semantics for hard-process, ISR, remnant, flavor selection, ratios, maxima, envelopes, and cumulative selection.
distinctions.public_reader_change: Already established insufficient by D1C and D1D-A.
distinctions.versioned_fork_maintenance: Creates a continuing upstream-integration and scientific-validation burden.

A_REPOSITORY_OWNED_PYTHIA_FORK_OR_PATCH.rationale: The negative D1D-A record does not supply the complete consumer evidence required to bound a fork or redesign.

distinctions.ordinary_positive_probability_generation: Requires valid nonnegative sampling probabilities and rates.
distinctions.signed_event_samples: Can represent cancellations between complete weighted events but do not repair invalid internal sampling steps.
distinctions.signed_final_event_weight: Cannot retroactively repair negative probabilities, denominators, maxima, categorical choices, or rejection sampling.
distinctions.signed_kernels_or_sudakovs: Would require a reviewed mathematical formulation and a generator designed to sample it.
distinctions.signed_matrix_element_contributions: Are not equivalent to signed PDFs entering every internal generator consumer.
distinctions.weighted_empirical_event_sets: Are compatible with set inference only after a coherent event-generation measure exists.

B_SIGNED_WEIGHT_GENERATOR_ARCHITECTURE.rationale: No reviewed mathematical construction establishes valid signed internal sampling for the present PDF family and full generator path.

alpha_s_routing.rationale: The official ISR documentation exposes PDF and alpha_s routing, but not signed-PDF consistency across every consumer.

beam_remnant_semantics.rationale: Beam-remnant machinery is documented; validity for signed internal PDF rates is not established.

hard_process_semantics.rationale: The official examples include neutral-current lepton-proton DIS with gamma/Z exchange.

isr_backward_evolution_semantics.rationale: ISR and PDF variation support are documented, but signed-kernel probability validity is not.

license_redistribution.rationale: Source and license files are public; any redistributed modification would still require a dedicated license review.

maintained_source_build_availability.rationale: An official maintained source repository and build documentation are available.

negative_rate_or_signed_weight_treatment.rationale: Primary literature supports negative final event weights in NLO matching, not negative PDFs inside all sampling kernels.

pointer_provider_coverage.rationale: The external PDF API exposes scalar accessors and copies; complete internal consumer coverage is not proven.

reproducibility.rationale: Versioned source and configuration are available, while the proposed signed contract has no validated identity record.

signed_pdf_scalar_preservation.rationale: No reviewed primary source proves signed scalar preservation through hard, ISR, and remnant consumers.

alpha_s_routing.rationale: Herwig 7.3 documents separate ISR and FSR alpha_s controls; complete PDF-provider coupling is unproven.

beam_remnant_semantics.rationale: The primary manual describes remnant construction, not signed-PDF validity.

hard_process_semantics.rationale: Herwig is documented for lepton-hadron hard scattering, but this exact fixed contract is not validated.

isr_backward_evolution_semantics.rationale: Backward-evolution shower semantics are documented; signed-kernel probability validity is not.

license_redistribution.rationale: The current software paper identifies GPLv3 availability; redistribution details require a dedicated review.

maintained_source_build_availability.rationale: The current software paper identifies maintained public source and build availability.

negative_rate_or_signed_weight_treatment.rationale: MC@NLO supports negative event weights, not negative probabilities in PDF-dependent shower/remnant steps.

pointer_provider_coverage.rationale: No bounded primary-source audit establishes provider coverage for the present signed PDF contract.

reproducibility.rationale: Versioned releases are documented, but no validated deterministic identity exists for this proposed coupling.

signed_pdf_scalar_preservation.rationale: No reviewed primary source proves signed scalar preservation through hard, ISR, and remnant consumers.

alpha_s_routing.rationale: The transport record does not own downstream alpha_s routing.

beam_remnant_semantics.rationale: Beam-remnant construction is delegated to the receiving generator.

hard_process_semantics.rationale: The standard transports hard parton-level configurations but does not validate this signed PDF contract.

isr_backward_evolution_semantics.rationale: Backward evolution is delegated and therefore cannot be repaired by the transported final weight.

license_redistribution.rationale: This entry evaluates an interchange standard rather than redistributing a generator.

maintained_source_build_availability.rationale: The interchange standard is not a generator implementation.

negative_rate_or_signed_weight_treatment.rationale: The standard carries event weights and MC@NLO establishes signed hard-event samples.

pointer_provider_coverage.rationale: A hard-event record is not a PDF provider interface.

reproducibility.rationale: The standardized record supports provenance fields, but downstream generator identity remains separate.

signed_pdf_scalar_preservation.rationale: The interface transports events, not the signed PDF scalar through generator internals.

C_ALTERNATIVE_GENERATOR_OR_TRANSPORT_INT.rationale: Sherpa and Herwig expose potentially relevant full-generator interfaces, while LHEF transports signed complete-event weights only; none proves the fixed signed-PDF contract end to end.

D_STOP_FURTHER_GENERATOR_COUPLING_WORK.rationale: Stopping current generator-coupling work protects the fixed D0R signed binary64 contract, theta box, shape-only fixed-N MVP, and hard/ISR/remnant consistency requirement. This is not a universal impossibility theorem and can be reopened only on new reviewed evidence.

failure_scope: No current architecture is authorized for the fixed signed D0R generator-coupling contract.
The minimal public-reader patch remains insufficient.
The rejected provenance slice remains diagnostic rather than architecture evidence.

fixed_scientific_contract.amortized_objective: p(theta_PDF | D) for a set of events D
fixed_scientific_contract.scalar_contract: signed binary64 x*f with strict support and no extrapolation

non_failure_scope: This decision is not a universal impossibility theorem for signed event generators.
It does not reject weighted empirical sets after a coherent event measure exists.
It does not alter the fixed PDF-family or inference contracts.

reopen_conditions.condition: A reviewed mathematical signed-kernel and signed-Sudakov formulation covering all internal sampling decisions.
A primary-source generator interface with proven signed scalar, rate, ISR, remnant, and event-weight semantics.
An independently validated complete consumer and dataflow graph for the proposed coupling.
A separately reviewed and approved change to the PDF-family or inference contract.

unresolved_evidence: No complete independently validated PDF-consumer graph is available.
No reviewed signed-kernel or signed-Sudakov probability construction is available.
Sherpa and Herwig primary sources do not prove signed scalar preservation through hard process, ISR, and remnants.
Full neutral-current gamma/Z, strict-support, provider, alpha_s, and concurrency behavior remain unvalidated for candidate alternatives.
Maintenance and redistribution costs are not sufficiently bounded across every potentially coherent route.
